ajnas.description: Saba has ambiguous size. This six-degree span follows the source illustration; it is not a claim that Saba is a fixed-size hexachord.
The source describes performance adjustments that narrow the written augmented second. These equal-tempered targets are notation approximations.
The tonic is the top note; placement is measured from the lowest note.

Secondary trichord form, as illustrated for Saba.

maqamat.description: Source-bounded Nikriz route, including the lowered eighth degree and the distinct upper-register third. It must not be repeated by octaves. Reference tonic: Re.

variants.description: Alternative degree eight is the natural tonic octave. This bounded illustration stops there; no further notes are inferred.

maqamat.description: Primary illustration uses Hijaz above the fifth. The Kurd alternative is separate; direction is not imposed as a universal rule. Reference tonic: Do.

variants.description: The seventh is lowered relative to the primary illustration.

maqamat.description: Egyptian Ajam illustration on Do. Upper Ajam resolves to the octave. A transposition is not automatically the distinct maqam Ajam Ushayran.

variants.description: The alternate upper jins lowers the seventh; shown independently from Upper Ajam.

maqamat.description: Bayati root with Nahawand above the fourth; Rast is another documented route. Reference tonic Re is a teaching example, not a restriction.

variants.description: The sixth rises by a notated quarter tone. For Bayati on La this is Fa half-sharp, not Fa half-flat.

maqamat.description: Plain Sikah illustration, not Huzam. The source describes it as a rare member of the family. Upper Rast spans the third to sixth degrees with its tonic at the sixth. Reference tonic: Mi half-flat.
Hijaz root with Nahawand above the fourth. Rast is a documented alternative. Written semitones and augmented seconds approximate performance intonation. Reference tonic: Re.

variants.description: The sixth rises by a notated quarter tone compared with the Nahawand route.

maqamat.description: Root Rast followed by Upper Rast resolving to the octave. The Nahawand upper route is distinct. Reference tonic: Do.

variants.description: The seventh is lowered relative to Upper Rast. The source illustrates this in descent without imposing an absolute direction rule.

maqamat.description: Kurd root followed by Nahawand above the fourth. Reference tonic: Re.

provenance.source: Research transcription of the scale illustrations and ajnas described by Johnny Farraj / MaqamWorld, cross-checked with Sami Asmar, Maqamat: Ascending Intervals & Transpositions (https://www.turath.org/Resources/MaqamTrans.htm). Accessed 2026-10-22. Cents are our 24-EDO conversion of written accidentals, NOT measured Arabic performance intonation. This project has not yet obtained musician validation or tested these hypotheses against labelled real performances. Per-entry source URLs are provided.
